summary: J. B. Disanayaka works in linguistics and Indology. He held a post at the University of Colombo from around 1968 to 2002 and is attested at SOAS University of London in 1996.

J. G. Jennings worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as Principal of Muir Central College and as Director of Public Instruction in the Department of Public Instruction, Bihar and Orissa, attested in 1918.

J. G. de Casparis (1916–2002) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar who taught David N. Lorenzen. He was a professor at Leiden University (attested 1987) and held an affiliation at SOAS University of London (attested 1991).

Religious studies scholar J. Gordon Melton studied at Birmingham-Southern College, Garrett-Evangelical Theological Seminary, and Northwestern University (Ph.D.). He founded the Institute for the Study of American Religion and held posts at UC Santa Barbara and Baylor University.
J. L. Shaw specializes in philosophy and Indology. He studied at Rice University and under Bimal Krishna Matilal, and held a post at Victoria University of Wellington from around 1972 to 2015.
J. M. E. McTaggart (1866–1925) was a philosopher who studied at Clifton College. He held a post at the University of Cambridge from around 1897 to 1923, where he taught Surendranath Dasgupta.
J. N. Farquhar (1861–1929) worked in Indology and religious studies. He was educated at Aberdeen Grammar School, the University of Aberdeen (~1883–1885), and Christ Church (~1885–1889).

J. Robert Oppenheimer studied at Harvard, Cambridge, and Göttingen, and studied under Arthur W. Ryder. His career included posts at UC Berkeley, Caltech, the Manhattan Project (1943–1945), and the Institute for Advanced Study (1947–1966).

J. S. Negi specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology, having studied under Ram Shankar Tripathi. He conducted research at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (attested 1977) and served as Chief Editor at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 1993–2001).
J. S. Pade was an Indology scholar who served as a Research Officer at the University of Chicago (attested 1963) and at the Oriental Institute, Vadodara (attested 1966).

Japanology scholar J. Thomas Rimer studied at Princeton and Columbia. He held academic posts at Washington University in St. Louis (~1971–1983), the University of Maryland, College Park (~1988–1997), the University of Pittsburgh (~1997–2010), and UCLA.

Jack Goody (1919–2015) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and religious studies. He studied at St Albans School and St John's College, Cambridge, and held a post at the University of Cambridge from around 1954 to 1984.
Jack Laughlin works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD from McMaster University in 1999 and held an academic post at the University of Sudbury.

Tibetologist Jacob Dalton earned his Ph.D. at the University of Michigan under Donald S. Lopez, Jr. He held posts at the British Library, SOAS, Yale University, and the University of California, Berkeley.

Jacob Grimm (1785–1863) studied at the University of Marburg and worked in linguistics. He held posts at the University of Göttingen (~1830–1837) and the University of Berlin (1841), and taught Leo Meyer.
Jacob Holubeck works in Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2013).
Jacob N. Kinnard is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. He has held academic posts at William & Mary as Assistant Professor of Religion and at the Iliff School of Theology.

Jacob Samuel Speyer (1849–1913) studied under Johan Hendrik Caspar Kern at Leiden University. He lectured at the University of Amsterdam, was professor of Latin at Groningen, and served as Professor of Indology at Leiden (1903–1913).

Indologist and linguist Jacob Wackernagel studied at Basel, Göttingen, Leipzig, and Oxford. He held chairs at the University of Basel (1879–1902, 1915–1936) and the University of Göttingen (1902–1915), and founded the Society for Indo-European Studies.

Jacqueline I. Stone studied at SFSU and UCLA, completing her Ph.D. under William R. LaFleur. Working in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies, she was a professor at Princeton University from 1990 to 2019.
